source.title: Deep learning versus kernel learning: an empirical study of loss landscape geometry and the time evolution of the Neural Tangent Kernel
source.authors: Stanislav Fort; G. Dziugaite; Mansheej Paul; Sepideh Kharaghani; Daniel M. Roy; S. Ganguli

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; some figure-axis text is garbled, but the relevant text descriptions and table details are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports training curves and compares training performance across ordinary and linearized training, datasets, architectures, and batch-normalization settings. These results bear on V1's prediction about training error, using the study's own training experiments rather than the original claim's explicit random-label or size sweeps.
record.gate_note: The study reports training-error curves for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 networks and linearized-training comparisons. Results cited from other studies in the introduction and references are not extracted. The paper does not report corrupted or random-label training.
record.test_reason: The study measures training classification error in randomly initialized convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/100, directly bearing on V1 using the same method and measure. The supplied text does not preserve readable curve endpoints, so it cannot establish whether training error reaches near zero.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but underspecified. The authors conclude that training undergoes an early chaotic-to-stable transition that determines basin fate; the evolving NTK rapidly learns useful features and matches full-network performance after 30–90 epochs. They also find that finite-width nonlinear training retains an early advantage over linearized training even at very low learning rates. They do not explicitly conclude that ordinary training reaches zero training classification error.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies training dynamics and linearized approximations, not memorization of corrupted or random labels; its experiments report training-error curves but do not provide textual endpoint values for them.
record.method_sensitivity: The experiments vary dataset, architecture, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and batch normalization. The authors report that training dynamics and linearized-training performance vary across these settings, but do not give textual training-error endpoints for the relevant curves.

fits_no_version.finding: Linearized models initialized from later training checkpoints outperform the initialization NTK and eventually match ordinary-network performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Features learned early by finite-width nonlinear networks improve subsequent fixed-kernel learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C.1 reports an early period with top Hessian eigenvalue above 2 divided by the learning rate, followed by declining curvature; Appendix C.2 discusses subsequent confinement within a local quadratic basin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Practical minibatch training can initially traverse regions whose curvature exceeds the quadratic gradient-descent stability threshold before settling into a basin.

record.problems: For the training-error curves relevant to V1, endpoints are presented only in plots and not described numerically in the text; several extracted row values are therefore figure-only and cannot be classified against the near-zero-error prediction. No corrupted-label or random-label setting is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Training-error plots for CIFAR-100 SimpleCNN or other figures are not separately reported in text or fully identifiable as distinct training-error results in the supplied figure text; the readable paper text does not support extracting additional values beyond the listed experiment curves.

untested.parts: Corrupted or random labels; systematic model-size comparisons; effects of early stopping and regularization on ordinary-network training error.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Controlled depth comparisons of plain and residual networks, longer training, and special initialization alternatives.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth. Using Kaiming initialization alone does not test these comparisons.
Recovery after an initial loss rise above the initial linearized stability limit, divergence boundaries, and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
Controlled comparisons of accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization, and the Fixup alternative.

missing.what: Ordinary ResNet20 training-error curves and epoch-200 reference errors for constant-learning-rate parent training on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. These are distinct from R1–R3's scheduled recipes or 160-epoch run. Values are unreadable in the supplied text, so no verdict follows.
missing.locator: Figure 8, train panels and caption; Appendix D.3

record.verdict_notes: No support, scope-limit, or challenge label is justified by unreadable training-error endpoints. Statements about low loss, matching performance, or disappearing interpolation barriers do not establish near-zero training classification error. The study is not an original source for V1.

versions.untested_parts: No corrupted or random labels, smaller-model comparison, or early-stopping/regularization sweep. Training error is plotted, but exact endpoint values are not given in readable text.
